newsitem.title: USA: Weld entitled to a hearing - Snowe.
newsitem.headline: Weld entitled to a hearing - Snowe.

text.p: William Weld, President Clinton's choice as U.S. ambassador to Mexico, is entitled to a confirmation hearing despite the opposition of Sen. Jesse Helms, Maine Republican Sen. Olympia Snowe said Thursday.
Snowe also said the White House had not pushed hard enough to get a hearing for Weld, who resigned Tuesday as governor of Massachusetts to campaign for confirmation.
Asked on NBC's "Today" show if Weld was entitled to a hearing, Snowe said: "Absolutely, and that's what this issue is all about. The (confirmation) process and making it work."
Helms, the powerful chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, opposes the nomination of his fellow Republican and has vowed to block a Senate confirmation vote.

Issues separating Helms and Weld include Weld's position on the use of marijuana for medicinal purposes. Helms has said he does not think Weld is of high enough calibre for the Mexico job and has cited his record on fighting drugs as one reason for opposing him.
Weld was scheduled to visit Capitol Hill Thursday to drum up support among senators for his nomination.
Snowe is among senators who have written to Helms, asking him to hold hearings on the nomination.

"The point of the letter is to demonstrate, along with 45 Democrats and eight Republicans, that Gov. Weld would have a majority in the United States Senate in support of confirmation as ambassador to Mexico," she said.

Criticising the White House for not pushing hard enough for a hearing, she said the administration should use this opportunity to clarify its drug policy and Weld should state what his drug policy toward Mexico would be.

"I don't think the administration has been playing a pivotal role. They should get behind this nominee. I can't imagine Secretary (of State Madeleine) Albright approaching Chairman Helms on this issue and saying this nominee is very important to us that he wouldn't reconsider."
White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry, at his daily news briefing on Wednesday, said Clinton would fight for Weld, describing him as "superbly qualified."
